```{r, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

RcmdrShiny keeps Rcmdr's command-generation semantics but replaces the Tk
interface with Shiny.  Most statistical work is unchanged; the differences are
in the interface and in extension points.

# What stays the same

- Commands are evaluated in the global environment (or an explicit
  environment when `run(env = ...)` is used).
- `Rcmdr-menus.txt` remains the menu source of truth.
- Commands such as `numSummary()`, `Tapply()`, `Anova()`, `scatterplot()` and
  `Confint()` are generated with the same arguments.
- Data sets, models and scripts are ordinary R objects.

# What changes

| Rcmdr | RcmdrShiny |
|---|---|
| Tk dialog windows | Bootstrap modals |
| Script and output windows | Script/Output/Messages/Plots/Data/Environment tabs |
| `showData()` window | Data tab with `DT` |
| `editDataset()` | `rhandsontable` below the cell threshold |
| `tcltk`/`tcltk2` | removed |
| Tk plugins | minimal Shiny plugin API |
| `identify()`/`locator()` | out of scope |

# Menus and activation

Menu entries are generated from `Rcmdr-menus.txt` and evaluated with Rcmdr's
activation predicates (for example `numericP()`, `factorsP()`,
`modelCapability()`).  Entries that are not available for the current data set
are disabled; unimplemented upstream entries are marked *In porting*.

# Plugins

Legacy `RcmdrPlugin.*` packages are detected but their Tk dialogs are not
executed.  New plugins use `RcmdrShiny.plugin()` with Rcmdr-style menu files,
direct commands and `plugin_dialog()` dialogs.  See the plugin vignette.

# Known limitations

- Gumbel distribution dialogs are unavailable (no base `qgumbel`/`pgumbel`).
- R Markdown/knitr document generation is not enabled.
- Interactive point identification is not implemented.
- The package targets a local single-user deployment; multi-user server
  isolation is out of scope.
